newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: HORSE RACING-SILVER PATRIARCH SEEKS CURRAGH COMPENSATION.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-SILVER PATRIARCH SEEKS CURRAGH COMPENSATION.

text.p: Silver Patriarch, narrow loser in one of the best Epsom Derby finishes for years, is even money favourite to pick up a major consolation prize on Sunday.
The English-trained colt is expected to face 11 rivals in the Irish Derby, raced over 12 furlongs at The Curragh.
Derby winner Benny The Dip and disappointing favourite Entrepreneur are staying at home. Benny The Dip is now considered more effective at 10 furlongs (2-km) and Entrepreneur is injured.
Silver Patriarch deserves to win after battling from a hopeless-looking situation at Epsom, where he was last with five furlongs (1-km) to travel, to be denied by the slimmest of margins.
Jockey Pat Eddery will be obliged to race the colt nearer the front and if he does Silver Patriarch has the necessary class.

But the Irish will not go down without a fight. Champion trainer Aidan O'Brien has decided to run Desert King (5-1), impressive winner of the 2,000 Guineas in Ireland before disapointing at Royal Ascot last week.
O'Brien also saddles Strawberry Roan (6-1), a shade unlucky in the Irish 1,000 Guineas when runner-up to Classic Park.
Frankie Dettori takes the ride and the fact that connections have paid a $100,000 late entry fee is a clear pointer that the filly is thought to have reasonable prospects.
O'Brien has a third string to his bow in the shape of Johan Cruyff (10-1), winner of his warm-up race at The Curragh on his reappearance early this month and an interesting runner.
Loup Sauvage (7-1), the French challenger, holds good place prospects as does The Fly, the other English raider, who finished a respectable fifth at Epsom.

Betting: Evens Silver Patriarch, 5-1 Desert King 6-1 Strawberry Roan, 7-1 Loup Sauvage, 10-1 Johan Cruyff, The Fly, 14-1 Token Gesture, 20-1 Casey Tibbs, Dr. Johnson, Verglas, 66-1 Olympic Majesty, 200-1 Buddy Marvel.
